chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: How head arrangements came about in the studio
summary: Basie starts a riff, the sections find their harmony, and the casual flip side often turns out to be the hit.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Describe how some of the head arrangements come about? How did that work?

Well, we would -- I'll tell you, we've gone to the studio, 16 pieces, and we'd have the first maybe one or two arrangements. And we'd just -- Basie would get with the rhythm section, start something, and the saxophones would get a line, just like a riff.
Would they get the line from Basie?

No, maybe somebody in the section, not all the time. But he has given lines sometimes and we'd all find our harmony and before we knew anything, we'd be doing this and the brass would be coordinating, you know, communicating in another way and the trombones would be doing -- then first thing you know, maybe after ten minutes, five or ten minutes, we got a terrific arrangement there. So then we'd stop. So Basie said, 'Now, here's what we do. We're going to record this.' And he'd say, 'Take the middle, Bud. Take the first eight, Bub,' you know, and that's the way we used -- you know, like --
Yeah, uh-huh. He used to take -- those would be like some kind of the head arrangement we would do on records and when you know anything, it would be swinging like

crazy, because I've seen -- I don't know, I can't recall particular tunes now, but I do know there are times we've gone to the studio and with a good fine arrangement and we would say, 'Well, this is the one that's going to really take off.' And on the -- we called them flip side on the other side because they were 78's, you know, -- on the other side would be the one that was the big seller that we hadn't spent any time with. So you --

Head arrangement, maybe Basie's rhythm section played a little bit and give Prez the solo and Sweets something here and you know, it wouldn't -- we hadn't spent any time with it, just something to, you know, to pass the time away. And that would be a big hit.
